taxonomy.infraspecific_note: Kew currently recognizes Juniperus ashei var. ashei and Juniperus ashei var. ovata. This review remains at species rank; do not assign a variety without separate evidence.

documented_counties.evidence: UT Plant Resources Center Natural Purola flora explicitly lists Juniperus ashei in the North Hays County flora.
Travis County Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly lists Ashe juniper.
USGS Honey Creek State Natural Area study explicitly documents Ashe juniper in Comal County.

target_zone_range.native_context: Kew and Flora of North America treat Juniperus ashei as native in Texas.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county presence inferred from source-pool membership or iNaturalist counts.

morphology.look_here_first: On adult foliage, look for tiny scale leaves with raised, nearly hemispheric dorsal glands; on female plants, confirm 6–9 mm dark-blue glaucous seed cones and shredding strip-like bark.
morphology.habit: Evergreen dioecious shrub or tree, commonly irregular to rounded; bark brown to gray and exfoliating in thin shredding strips.
morphology.leaves: Adult leaves scale-like, dark green, with finely denticulate margins; the abaxial gland is raised and hemispheric, especially obvious on whip leaves. Juvenile leaves are awl-like.
morphology.reproductive: Female seed cones mature in one year, ovoid to nearly globose, 6–9 mm, dark blue and glaucous, usually with one seed.
morphology.habitat: Limestone glades, bluffs, rocky shallow soils, oak-juniper woodland and savanna of Central Texas.

confusers.separator: FNA: J. virginiana has elliptic/elongate leaf glands and entire scale-leaf margins; its cones are usually smaller (3–6[–7] mm). Ashe juniper has raised hemispheric glands and denticulate margins.
FNA/Texas A&M: J. pinchotii has copper to copper-red nonglaucous cones and often white crystalline wax flecks on yellow-green leaves; Ashe juniper has deep blue glaucous cones and no such exudate.

photo_verification.note: UT Austin has a dedicated Juniperus ashei structures page with scanned glands, cones, seeds, juvenile leaves, adult leaves and whorls. UT BIO406D adds habit, bark and male/female cone views; USFS FEIS supplies a credited CC BY-NC cone/foliage field photo.
